title: Skills heatmap and micro-slice auction for cycle staffing and scope allocation
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Pilot a lightweight, skills-driven allocation process that uses a centralized skills heatmap and a timed micro-slice auction to assign engineers to cycle slices. Goal: make staffing decisions more transparent, surface latent capacity, and reduce high-friction mid-cycle reassignments.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Heatmap populated with at least 90% of contributors in scope and validated by managers; 2) Micro-slice auction ran for Cycle W11 and produced an allocation accepted by PM and Eng leads; 3) Post-allocation survey shows >=70% satisfaction with transparency; 4) No critical path outages attributable to understaffing during the cycle.
tasks:
1. Define skill categories and proficiency bands (PM + Eng leads)
2. Build heatmap input template and collection form (Google Sheets)
3. Run manager validation pass and synthesize heatmap
4. Design micro-slice auction rules and timers (reserve slots, max continuous hours)
5. Run auction in stakeholder workshop and record allocations
6. Publish allocation and update cycle board; add watchers for critical slices
7. Run end-of-cycle survey and capture learnings
decisions:
- Use self-reported proficiency with manager validation rather than time-consuming tests.
- Auction will be first-price sealed bids using points (not monetary) where teams nominate point allocations for slices.
- Reserve up to 20% headroom for emergency runway (unallocated pool).
tradeoffs:
- Pros: faster alignment, better visibility of skills, democratic allocation that surfaces interest.
- Cons: may favor well-networked engineers, requires manager oversight to avoid misallocations, adds process overhead for small cycles.
risks:
1) Over-indexing on declared skills vs. actual performance.
2) Auction favors teams with spare points leading to uneven distribution.
3) Managers push back on perceived loss of control.
4) Time spent running the process reduces delivery time in a tight cycle.
